prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production pixel-art sprite atlas for Stardew Valley 1.6, original regional-Brazil mod art.
Use the supplied wiki game sprites ONLY as reference for pixel density, dark coloured outlines, readable leaf clusters, top-left highlights, warm wood shading and side-on slight top-down farm-game view. Do not copy the original species. Make polished, charming, carefully clustered pixel art, NOT painterly or blurry. Transparent RGBA backdrop, isolated sprites, no ground discs, no cast shadows, no words, no labels, no dividing lines, no decoration, no watermark.
IMPORTANT TECHNICAL LAYOUT: portrait canvas 1024 by 1600, an INVISIBLE EXACT UNIFORM GRID with FOUR columns and FIVE rows, twenty equal 256x320 cells. Every cell contains exactly its prescribed isolated sprite with wide transparent padding. Each object entirely within its own cell. Match positions between corresponding trees. Roots stay centered. Work as low-resolution art with visible crisp square pixels, about 48px wide x 90px tall for adult trees, displayed enlarged.
Row 1 cells 1-4: full mature tree, SPRING / SUMMER / AUTUMN / WINTER in that order.
Row 2 cells 1-4: the corresponding four variants described below; identical geometry and same root positions as row 1.
Row 3 cell 1: tiny two-leaf sprout, cell 2: small leafy sapling, cell 3: larger juvenile sapling with wood trunk, cell 4: FOUR detached little leaf/needle debris icons arranged as a two-by-two group with a clean transparent gap between each.
Row 4 cell 1: cut stump, slightly top-down elliptical fresh wood top with growth rings, roots and bark, cell 2: SAME stump with bright olive moss, cell 3: the inventory seed, cell 4: the inventory product described below.
Row 5 cell 1: the extra item described below, cell 2: a few very fine branching dark-purple crack lines on transparency for overlaying a stump (mild damage), cell 3: same but medium damage, cell 4: same but heavy damage. Cracks only, NO wood surface behind them.
Mature trees: all must remain narrower than 48 logical pixels, clear long visible trunk below crown, roots on same center axis, trunk at least 7 logical pixels wide near base. Juveniles, seeds, leaves, stump and products must be simple enough to read as 16x16 icons or 16x32 juvenile sprites. Use about 20-30 deliberate colours per species, clean edges, no soft gradients, no smudging. The 20 cells MUST remain separate, no overlap.
SPECIES: Araucária — Araucaria angustifolia.
SPECIFIC ART: A distinctive mature Brazilian araucaria with a very tall straight brown scaled trunk and a broad candelabra / umbrella crown at the top. Layered horizontal branches with dense dark emerald needle rosettes, NOT a triangular Christmas pine. Spring fresh emerald tips, summer deep cool green, autumn olive green, winter evergreen crown with crisp powder-blue and white snow caps. The tiny young sapling is a miniature tiered conifer. Inventory seed is an elongated tapered chestnut-red pinhão with a pale ivory point. Product is golden-amber aromatic resin in a small rustic glass pot. Extra item row 5 column 1 is two pinhões.
ROW 2 VARIANTS: moss-covered copies: add vivid olive moss patches to the lower bark while keeping each season identical

SPECIES: Erva-mate — Ilex paraguariensis.
SPECIFIC ART: A lush compact rounded irregular crown of glossy serrated oval medium-green leaves, several visible curved branches, slender warm grey-brown trunk. Not an oak or maple. Spring lime tips, summer jade green, autumn muted olive with a few small dark reddish-purple berries, winter evergreen dark leaves with a light cap of white snow. Inventory seed is a few tiny tan seeds beside a dark red-purple round berry. Product is a green herbal extract inside a tiny rustic stoppered glass bottle. Extra item row 5 column 1 is a sprig of glossy oval green yerba-mate leaves.
ROW 2 VARIANTS: moss-covered copies: add olive moss patches to the lower bark while keeping each season identical

SPECIES: Bracatinga — Mimosa scabrella.
SPECIFIC ART: A delicate airy rounded crown of tiny feathery bipinnate lime and sage green leaf clusters, pale slender branched trunk, subtle creamy-yellow round flower clusters in spring. Inventory seed is three tiny polished dark-brown beanlike seeds and a short curved dry pod. Product is clear honey-gold resin in a rustic little glass pot. Extra item row 5 column 1 is a dry curved seed pod.

SPECIES: Jabuticabeira — Plinia cauliflora.
SPECIFIC ART: A majestic wide dense irregular rounded crown of small glossy laurel-like oval leaves, a strong slightly knotted dark cinnamon-brown trunk, low branching fork, clearly distinct from bracatinga and yerba mate. Inventory seed is a round glossy dark brown-black drupe with a small pale tan cup. Product is amber aromatic sap in a little rustic glass vial. Extra item row 5 column 1 is a small jabuticabeira leaf and berry.

SPECIES: Canela-preta — Ocotea catharinensis.
SPECIFIC ART: A tall elegant laurel tree with a vertically oval crown of large pointed lance-shaped leaves, deep green and cool blue-green shadows, dark almost black ridged bark and a narrow central fork. NOT jabuticabeira: this crown is narrower and taller, the bark much darker. Spring fresh jade leaf tips, summer dark glossy green, autumn dusky olive and a few wine-brown highlights while evergreen, winter leafy blue-green crown with small snow caps. Inventory seed is an oval purple-black berry with a warm brown seed and small stem. Product is rose-amber aromatic resin in a tiny rustic glass pot. Extra item row 5 column 1 is two long laurel leaves and a black berry.
ROW 2 VARIANTS: moss-covered copies: add olive moss patches to the lower bark while keeping each season identical

SPECIES: Butiazeiro — Butia eriospatha.
SPECIFIC ART: An authentic southern Brazilian butia palm, a sturdy short-to-medium thick brown trunk covered in diamond-shaped old leaf bases, a graceful crown of long arching blue-sage-green feather fronds. NOT a coconut tree: dense downward-curving pinnate fronds and a thick fibrous trunk. Spring sage-lime tips, summer cool jade green, autumn olive-sage, winter evergreen silvery green with restrained white frost/snow on upper fronds. Row 1 palm crowns have NO FRUIT. Inventory seed is a round tan-brown stone with fine dark pores. Product is a little cluster of vivid orange-yellow butia fruits with tiny stems. Extra item row 5 column 1 is a single orange-yellow butia.
ROW 2 VARIANTS: alternate fruit-bearing copies: spring and winter match row 1 with no fruit; summer and autumn have two visible hanging bunches of orange-yellow butia fruits under the crown. These are NOT moss variants
